counterfactual_rationale: The SM90 FP8 selector routed decode GEMMs to a slower torch._scaled_mm path and regressed H100/H200 throughput. Hardware-specific performance CI for the reported decode shapes would plausibly catch the bad routing rule.

The ROCm HIP sampler made DeepSeek responses repetitive and also triggered resource errors on a ROCm GPT-OSS setup. ROCm accuracy/serving CI over the HIP sampler path would plausibly reveal the sampler-specific failure.

On sm < 89 GPUs, Marlin repacked FP8 weights as int32 and MLA cast activations to that storage dtype, causing an unsupported scalar-type RuntimeError. A hardware matrix including pre-FP8 GPUs running Marlin FP8 MLA would plausibly catch the dtype bug.

Under DP attention and breakable prefill, the pooled-indexer bridge rejected logical top-k rows because padding expanded the token count. A DP/breakable-prefill serving test with uneven prompts would plausibly catch the logical-versus-padded shape mismatch.

The record describes torch-compile errors in an AMD AITER DeepSeek test and changes AITER/container integration. AMD CI that rebuilds the AITER image and runs the torch-compile MLA test would plausibly catch the failure, though the root detail is sparse.

The ROCm ConchLinearKernel received packed asymmetric zero-points in the wrong layout, causing HIP illegal memory access. A memcheck or reference test for asymmetric W4A16 zero-point layouts would plausibly flag the OOB access.

The diffusion ring_attention path crashed when using upstream FA3 during a multi-GPU Wan generation command. An end-to-end diffusion ring-attention test with upstream FA3 would plausibly catch the interface mismatch.

The VisionAttention mask cache lacked an upper bound and the discussion explicitly asked for an OOM case to verify the fix. A long-running multimodal serving test that varies masks and monitors cache growth would plausibly catch the availability failure.

ROCm MXFP4 MoE rounded TP-sharded expert dimensions from 384 to 512 on CDNA3, inflating weights by about 30 GiB/GPU and starving KV cache. MI300X/CDNA3 serving CI for the TP-sharded DeepSeek-V4-Pro configuration would plausibly expose the memory failure.

The LoRA MoE path asserted for FP8 base models because it selected the wrong expert implementation. A model-load or smoke-generation test for FP8 MoE with LoRA enabled would plausibly catch the bad dispatch.

ModelOpt quantized weights needed wrapping back into Parameter objects for the v1 torch.compile path. A compiled ModelOpt forward smoke test would plausibly expose the wrapper incompatibility before merge.

The XPU rotary embedding path crashed on an unexpected fused_set_kv_buffer_arg and then switched to the XPU kernel implementation. XPU backend CI covering RoPE with the full attention call signature would plausibly catch it.

The KTransformers MoE wrapper swallowed an AttributeError and stopped identifying the final layer, so deferral rules silently stopped applying. A KT model test checking final-layer expert deferral would plausibly catch the configuration integration bug.

The change routes all-valid masks to a faster unmasked attention kernel and the record frames the issue as GPU time and throughput rather than wrong output, crash, or severe outage. I treated it as a performance optimization outside the kernel-correctness definition.

The record title says W4AFP8 accuracy problem, but the body and discussion provide no symptom, root cause, or validation details. I could not confidently assign a failure class or validation counterfactual.

The MoE LoRA path indexed local expert buffers incorrectly under EP and failed to filter the -1 sentinel, producing OOB writes and illegal memory access. Memcheck or EP/per-expert-LoRA unit tests with sentinel IDs would plausibly catch it.

The GGUF dequantize kernels truncated int64 element counts to int and could leave large output regions uninitialized, disclosing stale GPU memory. Bounds/init checking on oversized tensor dimensions would plausibly expose the uninitialized output.

The ROCm AITER ASM prefill gather treated token-level KV indices as page-granular for page_size > 1, reading wrong slots. Reference tests varying page_size above 1 on the ASM path would plausibly catch the indexing mismatch.

The trtllm_mha MTP path cached SWA-pool state from the wrong pool and let SWA layers read full-pool indices out of the smaller SWA cache. A Gemma-4 MTP serving test on the Blackwell backend would plausibly reproduce the illegal memory access.

The FLA plugin path crashed because device-specific torch libraries were not resolved correctly for a cuda-like plugin device. CI or smoke tests on the plugin device backend would plausibly catch the crash.
DeepSeek-V3.2 with MTP in V1 mode crashed during warmup because NSA passed a list to repeat_interleave. A DeepSeek MTP startup test would plausibly exercise that backend call.

ROCm MoE weight loading for Qwen3-style models crashed with narrow() on a 0-dim tensor in fused_moe weight loading. ROCm model-load CI for those quantized MoE checkpoints would plausibly catch the loader/kernel-wiring bug.

Cutlass MLA with CUDA graphs yielded near-zero GSM8K accuracy while the non-CUDA-graph path was around normal accuracy. A full CUDA-graph Cutlass MLA serving/eval test would plausibly expose the bad graph integration.

GroupReduceMax used a fixed shuffle mask that relied on undefined behavior for the upper half of a warp. A static warp-mask analysis would plausibly flag the participating-lane mismatch before inputs happen to expose it.

The NVIDIA TRT-LLM FP4 MoE backend failed under MTP when some MoE layers were unquantized and required fallback to FusedMoE. A speculative MTP serve test with mixed quantized and unquantized MoE layers would plausibly catch the dispatch error.

Sparse MLA on SM90 used the wrong index_kpool setting, leaving query tokens unread at positions past 2048 and corrupting tool-call-heavy sessions. Targeted attention tests varying position and index_kpool would plausibly catch the mismatch.

ROCm TritonMLA advertised CUDA-graph support that allowed full decode capture with max_query_len=2, tripping a decode-only assertion. ROCm speculative-decoding initialization tests would plausibly catch the invalid CUDA-graph support level.

The ROCm MLA fallback had incompatible flash-attn/vllm_flash_attn interface assumptions after adjacent PRs changed arguments. ROCm MLA backend tests across the flash-attn interface versions would plausibly catch the incompatibility, though the record gives limited symptom detail.

The RMSNorm kernels multiplied by weights in FP32 rather than the weight's BF16/FP16 dtype, compounding per-layer errors until only about 2% of output tokens matched reference. Kernel-vs-Python dtype reference tests across layernorm variants would plausibly catch it.

ROCm AITER attention advertised FULL CUDA graph mode even though prefill and decode use different kernels, leading to OOMs and accuracy issues. Full serving tests with ROCm AITER and FULL/Piecewise CUDA-graph capture would plausibly expose the bad support declaration.
